pages.text: The controller is the routing hub of a $(l:ae2_mechanics/me_network_connections)ME Network$(/l). Without it, a network is "ad-hoc" and can only have a max of 8 channel-using $(l:ae2_mechanics/devices)devices$(/l) total.$(br2)It is not possible to have 2 controllers in one $(l:ae2_mechanics/me_network_connections)ME Network$(/l).$(br2)The controller provides 32 $(l:ae2_mechanics/channels)Channels$(/l) per face.

The controller requires 6 AE/t per controller block to function. Each controller block can store 8000 AE, so larger networks might require additional energy storage. See $(l:ae2_mechanics/energy)energy$(/l) for details.$(br2)Multiblock Controllers can be built in a fairly free form.
However, there are a few rules that must be followed:

1. All controller blocks on a $(l:ae2_mechanics/me_network_connections)ME Network$(/l) must be connected; else the blocks will turn red.$(br2)2. The size of the controller must be within 7x7x7; else it will turn red.$(br2)3. A controller can have 2 adjacent blocks in at most 1 axis; if a block violates this rule, it will disable and turn red.$(br2)$(#555)$(o)(3D scene not available in this version)$()

As long as all rules are followed and powered, the controller should glow and cycle colors.$(br2)You can right-click on a controller to get the same GUI as a $(l:items_blocks_machines/network_tool)Network Tool$(/l)
